title: Topic-level knowledge checks and concept questions
learningObjectives: Explain the concept or reference contract.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify relevant assumptions and edge cases.
Apply the skill in a documented exercise.

understand.concept: Topic-level checks assess whether learners can explain definitions, identify valid constructs, trace code and recognize common misconceptions. Questions should align with the lesson objectives and include explanations for correct answers.
understand.whyItMatters: Short feedback loops help learners detect misunderstandings before they build on them in later topics.
understand.analogy: Treat a reference or learning task as a contract that states what is expected and how success is checked.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard or library specification.

explain.narrative:
Topic-level checks assess whether learners can explain definitions, identify valid constructs, trace code and recognize common misconceptions. Questions should align with the lesson objectives and include explanations for correct answers.

Use authoritative declarations and documentation, state assumptions explicitly and verify behaviour with focused examples. Where the implementation or C version matters, record it.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The expression x++ yields the old value for y, then increments x. A useful knowledge check asks learners to predict both values and explain the sequencing.

practise.guidedTask: Write one concept question and one code-tracing question for a topic you have studied.
practise.independentTask: Create five questions with plausible distractors and explanations for every answer.
hints: Distractors should target real misconceptions, not ambiguous wording.
Test whether the question has one clearly defensible answer.
Align each question with a stated learning objective.
